description: Web Threat Defense User Service helps protect your computer by warning the user when unauthorized entities attempt to gain access to their credentials
why: Per-user Web Threat Defense. Merged per-user instances: webthreatdefusersvc_1a2b3c. Measured working set about 4.5 MB (own process).

description: This service manages persistent subscriptions to events from remote sources that support WS-Management protocol. This includes Windows Vista event logs, hardware and IPMI-enabled event sources.
why: Windows Event Collector (event forwarding); demand-start. Not running at inventory time.

description: Windows Encryption Provider Host Service brokers encryption related functionalities from 3rd Party Encryption Providers to processes that need to evaluate and apply EAS policies. Stopping this will compromise EAS compliancy checks that have been established by the connected Mail Accounts
why: Windows Encryption Provider Host; demand-start. Not running at inventory time.

description: This service provides support for viewing, sending and deletion of system-level problem reports for the Problem Reports control panel.
why: Problem Reports control panel support; already Disabled. Not running at inventory time.

description: Allows errors to be reported when programs stop working or responding and allows existing solutions to be delivered. Also allows logs to be generated for diagnostic and repair services.
why: Windows Error Reporting; already Disabled here. Crash reports for debugging are lost while disabled. Not running at inventory time.

description: Monitors the device for a better user experience
why: Windows Health and Optimized Experiences; newer service, scope unclear. Measured working set about 14.0 MB (own process).

description: Launches applications associated with still image acquisition events.
why: Still Image acquisition events; no scanner, demand-start. Not running at inventory time.

description: WinHTTP implements the client HTTP stack and provides developers with a Win32 API and COM Automation component for sending HTTP requests and receiving responses. In addition, WinHTTP provides support for auto-discovering a proxy configuration via its implementation of the Web Proxy Auto-Discovery (WPAD) protocol.
why: WinHTTP proxy auto-discovery; networking stacks depend on it. Measured working set about 6.3 MB (own process).

description: Provides a common interface and object model to access management information about operating system, devices, applications and services. If this service is stopped, most Windows-based software will not function properly.
why: WMI; many tools, Defender and Bitdefender depend on it. RAM impact not measured (shared svchost or unknown).

description: Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service implements the WS-Management protocol for remote management. WS-Management is a standard web services protocol used for remote software and hardware management.
why: Remote management endpoint for inbound PowerShell remoting. Demand-start. Not running at inventory time.

description: Provides infrastructure support for the Windows Insider Program. This service must remain enabled for the Windows Insider Program to work.
why: Windows Insider Service; only for Insider builds. Demand-start. Not running at inventory time.

description: The WLANSVC service provides the logic required to configure, discover, connect to, and disconnect from a wireless local area network (WLAN) as defined by IEEE 802.11 standards. It also contains the logic to turn your computer into a software access point so that other devices or computers can connect to your computer wirelessly using a WLAN adapter that can support this.
why: WLAN AutoConfig; Wi-Fi does not work without it. Measured working set about 5.4 MB (own process).
sources: local: sc qc/qdescription + Win32_Service (DisplayName=WLAN AutoConfig; StartMode=Auto) + VersionInfo of wlansvc.dll (CompanyName=Microsoft Corporation; FileDescription=Windows WLAN AutoConfig Service DLL)

description: Enables user sign-in through Microsoft account identity services. If this service is stopped, users will not be able to logon to the computer with their Microsoft account.
why: Microsoft Account Sign-in Assistant; Store/Xbox/Microsoft account sign-in. Not running at inventory time.

description: Enforces group policy for removable mass-storage devices. Enables applications such as Windows Media Player and Image Import Wizard to transfer and synchronize content using removable mass-storage devices.
why: Portable Device Enumerator; phones, cameras and USB MTP devices. Not running at inventory time.

description: This service runs in session 0 and hosts the notification platform and connection provider which handles the connection between the device and WNS server.
why: Push notifications system service; toasts, Store and many apps. RAM impact not measured (shared svchost or unknown).

description: This service hosts Windows notification platform which provides support for local and push notifications. Supported notifications are tile, toast and raw.
why: Per-user push notifications; notification center and toasts. Merged per-user instances: WpnUserService_1a2b3c. Measured working set about 22.8 MB (own process).

description: Windows AI Components Host (AI Fabric) service: hosts Windows AI components for apps and other Windows services and launches WorkloadsSessionHost.exe processes.
why: Hosts Windows AI workloads (Copilot, Recall, Click to Do, AI search in Settings). A Microsoft Q&A moderator suggests Manual as a workaround when those features are not used; other users report about 5 GB RAM in idle WorkloadsSessionHost.exe on 25H2 (not measured here; the service process itself measured about 1.9 MB). Stopping it disables those AI features only; Office, apps and Windows Update are unaffected per the same thread.

description: The WSCSVC (Windows Security Center) service monitors and reports security health settings on the computer. The health settings include firewall (on/off), antivirus (on/off/out of date), antispyware (on/off/out of date), Windows Update (automatically/manually download and install updates), User Account Control (on/off), and Internet settings (recommended/not recommended).
why: Security Center; reports AV/firewall status (Bitdefender registration). Measured working set about 7.2 MB (own process).
sources: local: sc qc/qdescription + Win32_Service (DisplayName=Security Center; StartMode=Auto) + VersionInfo of wscsvc.dll (CompanyName=Microsoft Corporation; FileDescription=Windows Security Center Service)

description: Provides content indexing, property caching, and search results for files, e-mail, and other content.
why: Windows Search indexer; already Disabled here. Start menu and Explorer search fall back to slow non-indexed search. Not running at inventory time.

description: Enables the detection, download, and installation of updates for Windows and other programs. If this service is disabled, users of this computer will not be able to use Windows Update or its automatic updating feature, and programs will not be able to use the Windows Update Agent (WUA) API.
why: Windows Update. Not running at inventory time.

why: Usage and quality insights; drives self-healing and personalized offers. Self-healing link makes it not clearly safe to disable. Not running at inventory time.
